usage: jbus queue add [-h] --priority PRIORITY [--depends DEPENDS]
                      [--merge-after MERGE_AFTER] [--entry ENTRY]
                      [--item ITEM] [--from THREAD] [--for HOME]
                      [--message THREAD/MESSAGE]
                      slug

Queue a row, with its brief on stdin. A follow-up: a row is a follow-up of the
row P, and jbus approves it by the follow-up rule (a follow-up of approved
work needs no new approval) when it is queued and on each pass, when it names
P (its brief's head has a line `Follows: P`), when its brief holds no case of
gates.md, when it is queued (by a home, with or without --entry) or is a fix
jbus filed (a row jbus's pass queued whose brief's Decisions: line begins
`none, jbus filed this from a red `), and when P's go holds (P is a row of the
queue, or went as merged, and its go is the user's word or this rule's); a fix
jbus filed that names no parent is approved by the same rule on the red run
its brief's Task: line quotes, and the day's warnings row, a row jbus's pass
queued whose brief's Decisions: line begins `none, jbus filed this from the
warnings of later reviews`, on the later reviews that line names; any other
row waits for the user's go.

positional arguments:
  slug

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --priority PRIORITY   an integer, lower first
  --depends DEPENDS     slugs that must be merged before this row launches,
                        with commas: each one the brief's Builds on: line
                        names
  --merge-after MERGE_AFTER
                        slugs whose pull requests merge before this row's,
                        with commas: jmerge waits
  --entry ENTRY         the plan entry the row is work for, when not its own
                        slug
  --item ITEM           the work item the row is, by its id; with none, one is
                        made
  --from THREAD         the thread of the home that adds the row, empty for
                        the uncategorized home: a brief whose Home: line names
                        another home is refused, and the root home, which owns
                        no row, gives --for
  --for HOME            the scope the brief's Home: line resolves to,
                        uncategorized where it names no scope: the row is that
                        home's, handed over on purpose
  --message THREAD/MESSAGE
                        the user's own message in T3 Code that gives the go
                        for this brief: the row is approved on it in the same
                        write, as queue approve --message approves it
